derivations.quote: At each source, gate and sink $v$, assign an invertible $R$-linear operator $D_v$ on $R^\Omega$, called its frame. A frame may mix entries of one array across addresses, whereas a gate combines different wires at one fixed address. All incidences of a gate use the same $D_v$, and an edge from $u$ to $v$ applies $D_vD_u^{-1}$ to the array it carries.

The invariant is that the stored array at $v$ equals $D_v$ applied to the logical array. It holds at the sources by definition: with $D_{\rm in}=\bigoplus_w D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}$ stacking the source frames over the input roles $w$, a physical input $f$ is interpreted as the logical input $g=D_{\rm in}^{-1}f$, which needs no preprocessing. It continues along an edge: if the logical array is $\varphi$, the stored array $D_u\varphi$ becomes $D_vD_u^{-1}D_u\varphi=D_v\varphi$.
Because $D_v$ is $R$-linear, $\sum_j c_jD_v\varphi_j=D_v\bigl(\sum_j c_j\varphi_j\bigr)$. So $G(D_vg_1,\dots,D_vg_t)=D_vG(g_1,\dots,g_t)$ for any arrays $g_1,\dots,g_t$
With $D_{\rm out}=\bigoplus_w D_{\mathrm{sink}(w)}$, the implemented operator is therefore

So if the scalar network is a signed role permutation sending input role $w$ to output role $\rho(w)$ with scalar sign $\varepsilon_w$, that route applies $\varepsilon_wD_{\mathrm{sink}(\rho(w))}D_{\mathrm{source}(w)}^{-1}$ to its input array. This holds for every role, scratch roles included.

symbols.quote: At a gate $G$ with $t$ input arrays, every incoming array has the common frame $D_v$, and a gate output combines the logical inputs $\varphi_1,\dots,\varphi_t$ with coefficients $c_j\in R$.
